query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Semantic categorization of free-text short_description gives a strong grouping axis for analyzing incident distribution. Values (printer, network_connectivity, database) are well-grounded in the source text.

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: A distinct axis (what went wrong) that complements category and enables symptom-based analysis. Extractions like connectivity_failure and not_responding are sound readings of the text; NULLs for silent rows are acceptable. Slight risk of over-specific inference (e.g. 'not_responding' from 'not working properly'), but reasonable.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Useful for asset-level grouping, though it overlaps heavily with incident_category (printer/printer, network_connectivity/network_device). Still offers some independent leverage (e.g. database->software_application). Values are warranted from the text.

per_column.name: software_trigger
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean flag with heavy skew (446 false). Provides limited leverage and is partly redundant with category=software. Groundedness is defensible from text but the specific inference of whether software 'triggered' an incident is often not stated, risking confident defaults to False.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Not supported by the source text shown; short_description gives no indication of resolution mode. The 'True' for the floor-3 connectivity row appears to be an invented specific with no grounding. Weak analytical value as a poorly-grounded boolean.

judge.rationale: The categorical columns (incident_category, incident_symptom_type, affected_asset_type) turn unstructured short_description text into strong, well-grounded grouping axes directly serving the exploratory query, though asset_type partially overlaps category. The two boolean flags are weaker: software_trigger is skewed and semi-redundant, and self_resolved is not derivable from the available text and shows an unsupported 'True' assertion, dragging groundedness down.
